rationale: The workflow already bounds the e2e job with timeout-minutes: 20 and cancels superseded runs via concurrency cancel-in-progress, but the format, lint, typecheck, and test jobs have no explicit timeout, so a hung job can consume the default runner budget. This matches pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout), which is supported by measured CI workflow evidence: experiment batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 (26.82% elapsed savings) and experiment batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8 (9.79% elapsed savings) both added timeout-minutes to jobs while keeping all steps and checks passing. I add timeout-minutes: 20 to the four unbound jobs, reusing the same bound already present for e2e rather than inventing a new value. No steps, permissions, secrets, network access, or deployment operations are changed, so build/test coverage is preserved and no new privileged actions are introduced.
